inlines.v: Hiram sends artificers and materials to David, to build him a house, , . David's wives and children, . He defeats the Philistines in two battles: one in the valley of Rephaim, ; and the other at Gibeon and Gazer, . His fame goes out into all the surrounding nations, .
Now Hiram king of Tyre - See the transactions of this chapter related (note).

These are the names of his children - In (note), eleven persons only are mentioned in the Hebrew text, but the Septuagint has twenty-four, here there are thirteen, and all the versions have the same number, with certain varieties in the names. - See the notes there.
The Philistines went up to seek David - See on (note).
David inquired of God - "David consulted the Word of the Lord." - T.
Like the breaking forth of waters - "And David said, The Lord hath broken the enemies of David like to the breaking of a potter's vessel full of water." - T.

A sound of going - "When thou shalt hear the sound of the angels coming to thy assistance, then go out to battle; for an angel is sent from the presence of God, that he may render thy way prosperous." - T.
Into all lands - That is, all the surrounding or neighboring lands and nations, for no others can possibly be intended.
